body:
Quick answer

  • Formester for an all-rounder with AI + offline + payments.
  • Typeform for conversational lead-gen with the best perceived UX.
  • Tally for the most generous free tier (unlimited forms + responses).
  • Jotform for the biggest template library or HIPAA needs.
  • Paperform if your form reads more like a document.
  • Fillout if your forms tie into Airtable / Notion / Sheets as the data layer.

Drag-and-drop builders that ship in minutes, not weeks. Tested for real workflows: lead capture, payments, surveys, internal ops, and field data collection.

The best no-code form builders in 2026 are tools that let you build, brand, and ship a form in under 10 minutes without writing a line of code. The strongest options are Formester (best all-rounder with AI generation, offline support, and a real free tier), Jotform (biggest template library), Typeform (best conversational UX), Tally (cheapest with most features in the free tier), and Paperform (best for document-style forms). The 10 below cover lead capture, payments, surveys, conditional logic, and internal-ops use cases.

1Editor's pick

Formester: Best all-rounder (AI + offline + payments in one)

Best for: SMBs and growing teams that want one tool for lead capture, surveys, payments, and offline data collection without enterprise pricing.

What makes it stand out

  • AI form generator powered by Google Gemini: describe the form in plain English, get a working form in seconds
  • Native offline mode: forms cache in the browser, sync on reconnect
  • Real-time team collaboration on the Business plan
  • Native Stripe + PayPal payments with AES-256 encryption
  • Honest free tier: 100 responses/month, unlimited forms, no submission-cap throttling
  • Conditional logic, file uploads (100MB free / 1GB Personal), partial submissions, kiosk mode

Pricing

  • Free Plan: Yes (100 responses/month, unlimited forms)
  • Starting Price: $13/month Personal ($12/month annual)
  • Most Popular Plan: $49/month Business ($45/month annual)
  • Enterprise Plan: Custom pricing
  • Free Trial: No (free plan available instead)
  • Response Limits: 100 (free) / 5,000 (Personal) / 15,000 (Business)
  • Storage: 100MB free / 1GB Personal / 50GB Business
  • Team Collaboration: Business plan and above
ProsOne of the rare tools that combines AI generation, offline, payments, and real-time collaboration without each being a separate add-on. Free tier is genuinely usable.
ConsSmaller template library than Jotform. Not HIPAA-certified (GDPR / UK GDPR / CCPA only).
Try Formester free →
2

Jotform: Biggest template library, HIPAA-eligible

Best for: Teams that want a template for every imaginable form and may need HIPAA compliance.

What makes it stand out

  • 10,000+ pre-built templates
  • HIPAA-eligible on Gold ($99/mo) and higher
  • 100+ native integrations (Salesforce, HubSpot, Slack, Mailchimp)
  • AI form builder + Jotform Sign (e-signature add-on)
  • Native iOS + Android apps with offline mode

Pricing

  • Free Plan: Yes (100 submissions/month, 5 forms)
  • Starting Price: $34/month Bronze
  • Most Popular Plan: $39/month Silver
  • Enterprise Plan: Custom pricing (HIPAA available on Gold and Enterprise)
  • Free Trial: No (free plan available instead)
  • Submission Limits: 100 (free) / 1,000 (Bronze) / 2,500 (Silver) / 10,000 (Gold)
  • Form Limit: 5 (free) / 25 (Bronze) / 50 (Silver) / 100 (Gold)
  • HIPAA: Gold tier and above
ProsMost mature feature set. Most templates. HIPAA available.
ConsRestrictive free tier (5 forms cap). UI feels dated. Pricing climbs fast.
3

Typeform: Best conversational form UX

Best for: Marketing teams that want forms that feel like a conversation, one question at a time, higher completion rates on long-ish surveys.

What makes it stand out

  • One-question-per-screen format ("the Typeform feel")
  • Best-in-class video + image rendering
  • Native integrations: HubSpot, Mailchimp, Salesforce, Slack
  • Logic jumps with visual flowchart editor
  • Limited AI assistance for question writing

Pricing

  • Free Plan: Yes (10 responses/month, 1 form)
  • Starting Price: $29/month Basic ($28/month annual)
  • Most Popular Plan: $79/month Plus ($56/month annual)
  • Enterprise Plan: Custom pricing (Growth Flow tier and above)
  • Free Trial: No (free plan available instead)
  • Response Limits: 10 (free) / 100 (Basic) / 1,000 (Plus) / 10,000 (Business)
  • Pricing Save: 30% off with annual billing
ProsHighest perceived UX. Strong for B2C surveys and quizzes. Brand recognition.
ConsFree tier barely usable. Expensive at scale. Wrong for long internal forms.
4

Tally: Most generous free tier

Best for: Bootstrapped founders, indie hackers, and small teams that need unlimited forms + unlimited submissions for free.

What makes it stand out

  • Unlimited forms + unlimited responses on the free plan
  • Notion-style editor: type to add fields, slash commands
  • Clean modern design out of the box
  • Payments (Stripe), conditional logic, integrations all included on free

Pricing

  • Free Plan: Yes (unlimited responses + unlimited forms)
  • Starting Price: $24/month Pro
  • Most Popular Plan: $24/month Pro
  • Enterprise Plan: $74/month Business
  • Free Trial: No (free plan covers most use cases)
  • Responses: Unlimited on every tier
  • Forms: Unlimited on every tier
  • Branding Removal: Pro tier
ProsGenuinely the most generous free plan in the category. Modern UX. Fast to use.
ConsNo native mobile app. Limited templates. Branded on free ("Made with Tally"). Logic editor is text-only, not visual.
5

Paperform: Best for document-style forms

Best for: Forms that read like a document, long-form intake, applications, mortgage / loan forms, where layout matters more than question-by-question pacing.

What makes it stand out

  • Block-based document editor (text, images, fields mix freely)
  • Strong AI-assisted form builder
  • Native payments (Stripe, Square, Braintree)
  • Smart logic with calculations + workflows

Pricing

  • Free Plan: No
  • Starting Price: $24/month Essentials ($288/year)
  • Most Popular Plan: $49/month Pro ($588/year)
  • Enterprise Plan: $99/month Business ($1,188/year)
  • Free Trial: Yes (7 days, no credit card)
  • Submissions: 1,200/year (Essentials) / 12,000/year (Pro) / 120,000/year (Business)
  • Users: 1 (Essentials) / 3 (Pro) / 5 (Business, +$9/user up to 25)
ProsBest layout flexibility. Strongest for non-standard form layouts.
ConsNo free plan. Steeper learning curve than Tally or Formester.
6

Fillout: Best modern challenger with native data layer

Best for: Teams that want forms tightly coupled with a database (Airtable, Notion, Google Sheets).

What makes it stand out

  • Native integrations with Airtable, Notion, Google Sheets as data backends
  • AI form generator
  • Multi-step / scheduling forms with conditional logic
  • 1,000 free responses/month: most generous after Tally

Pricing

  • Free Plan: Yes (1,000 responses/month, unlimited forms)
  • Starting Price: $15/month Starter
  • Most Popular Plan: $40/month Pro
  • Enterprise Plan: $75/month Business
  • Free Trial: No (free plan covers basics)
  • Response Limits: 1,000 (free) / 5,000 (Starter) / 25,000 (Pro) / 100,000 (Business)
  • Per-Seat Charges: None, invite your whole company
ProsBest Airtable / Notion integration. Modern UX. Fair pricing.
ConsSmaller integration list than Jotform. Newer tool, less mature ecosystem.
7

Wufoo: Simple classic, owned by SurveyMonkey

Best for: Teams that want a stable, predictable form builder without learning a new UX.

What makes it stand out

  • Battle-tested since 2006
  • Clean simple UI
  • Native payments, conditional logic, file uploads

Pricing

  • Free Plan: Yes (100 entries/month, 5 forms)
  • Starting Price: $16.25/month Starter (annual billing)
  • Most Popular Plan: $33.25/month Professional (annual billing)
  • Enterprise Plan: $210.25/month Ultimate (annual billing)
  • Free Trial: No (free plan available instead)
  • Form Limit: 5 (free) / 10 (Starter) / Unlimited (Professional and up)
  • Annual Savings: 25% off vs monthly billing
ProsReliable. Easy onboarding. Good documentation.
ConsHasn't kept up with modern competitors on UX. No AI. Templates feel dated.
8

Google Forms: When the budget is zero and you don't need payments

Best for: Internal use cases inside Google Workspace, team polls, event RSVPs, classroom surveys.

What makes it stand out

  • Free for everyone with a Google account
  • Native Google Sheets integration (auto-creates the response sheet)
  • Gemini AI in Google Workspace can generate questions
  • Unlimited forms and submissions

Pricing

  • Free Plan: Yes (unlimited forms, no payments)
  • Starting Price: Free
  • Most Popular Plan: Free (Google Workspace from $6/user/month)
  • Enterprise Plan: Custom (Google Workspace Enterprise)
  • Free Trial: Not applicable
  • Form Limit: Unlimited
  • Native Payments: Not supported
  • Conditional Logic: Limited on free; full with Workspace
ProsFree, reliable, tight Google ecosystem integration.
ConsNo payments. Limited branding. No conditional logic on free tier. Generic Google look. Not built for customer-facing forms.
9

Microsoft Forms: When you're already on Microsoft 365

Best for: Internal users inside Microsoft 365, quick polls, internal surveys, basic intake forms.

What makes it stand out

  • Included with Microsoft 365 Business Standard ($12.50/user/mo) and higher
  • Copilot AI form generation (in Forms Pro)
  • Native Excel + Power Automate integration
  • Strong for educators with M365 Education

Pricing

  • Free Plan: Included with Microsoft 365 subscription
  • Starting Price: $6/user/month (M365 Business Basic)
  • Most Popular Plan: $12.50/user/month (M365 Business Standard)
  • Enterprise Plan: $23/user/month (M365 E3) or $38/user/month (M365 E5)
  • Free Trial: Yes (30 days on M365 Business plans)
  • Standalone Pricing: Not available as standalone product
  • AI Generation: Copilot in Forms Pro
  • Native Payments: Not supported
ProsFree if you're already on M365. Zero learning curve for Office users.
ConsNot customer-facing. No payments. Limited template library. No real branding.
10

Zoho Forms: Inside the Zoho ecosystem

Best for: Teams already paying for Zoho CRM, Zoho Books, or Zoho Desk.

What makes it stand out

  • Native Zoho ecosystem integration
  • Cheapest paid plan at $10/mo
  • Conditional logic, file uploads, payments (Stripe, PayPal, Authorize.net)
  • Multi-language support

Pricing

  • Free Plan: Yes (3 forms, 500 submissions/month)
  • Starting Price: $10/month Basic (annual billing)
  • Most Popular Plan: $25/month Standard (annual billing)
  • Enterprise Plan: $90/month Premium (annual billing)
  • Free Trial: Yes (15 days on paid plans)
  • Form Limit: 3 (free) / 25 (Basic) / Unlimited (Standard+)
  • Submissions: 500/month (free) / 10,000 (Basic) / 25,000 (Standard) / 100,000 (Premium)
ProsTight Zoho integration. Cheapest paid tier in the category.
ConsUI feels dated. Limited template library. Branding removal requires a higher tier.

Frequently asked questions

Common questions about no-code form builders, pricing, AI, and integrations.

What is a no-code form builder?
A no-code form builder is a tool that lets non-developers create web forms by dragging and dropping fields (text, email, dropdown, file upload, signature) into a visual editor. No HTML, CSS, or JavaScript required. The tool handles form rendering, validation, submission storage, and integrations with email/CRM/Sheets.
Are no-code form builders free?
Most have a free tier. The most generous free tiers in 2026 are Tally (unlimited forms + responses) and Formester (100 responses/mo, unlimited forms). Jotform, Typeform, and Wufoo cap free tiers at 10-100 responses/month. Google Forms and Microsoft Forms are free if you're already on Google Workspace or Microsoft 365.
What's the difference between no-code and low-code form builders?
No-code form builders require zero code, drag fields, configure logic in a visual editor, ship. Low-code form builders let you add custom JavaScript, CSS, or webhook logic when you outgrow the visual editor. For 95% of users, no-code is enough.
Which no-code form builder is best for AI?
Formester, Jotform, Typeform, Paperform, and Fillout all ship AI form generators in 2026. Formester's runs on Google Gemini and accepts plain-text prompts, paste-in question lists, or PDF uploads. Jotform's AI also supports prompt + PDF. Output quality is comparable; the differentiator is whether the AI works with the rest of the platform.
Can no-code form builders collect payments?
Yes. Formester (Stripe + PayPal), Jotform (Stripe, PayPal, Square + 30 others), Typeform (Stripe), Tally (Stripe), Paperform (Stripe + Square + Braintree), Fillout (Stripe), Wufoo (Stripe + PayPal), and Zoho Forms (Stripe, PayPal, Authorize.net) all support payments natively. Google Forms and Microsoft Forms do not.
Which no-code form builder has the best conditional logic?
Formester, Jotform, Typeform, Paperform, and Fillout all handle visual conditional logic well. Typeform's flowchart editor is the most visual. Formester's logic editor handles multi-condition rules (if X AND Y → show Z) without code. Tally's logic is text-only.
Are no-code forms secure?
Yes, with the right tool. Look for HTTPS-only submissions, GDPR / CCPA compliance, AES-256 encryption at rest, and SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification (for enterprise needs). Formester is GDPR / UK GDPR / CCPA compliant with AES-256 on the payments layer; Jotform offers HIPAA on Gold+; Typeform and Tally are GDPR-compliant but not SOC 2 or HIPAA certified.
Can I embed a no-code form on my website?
Yes, every tool listed supports iframe and JavaScript embed. Formester ships six embed modes (inline, popup, sidebar, side tab, popover, fullscreen). Jotform and Typeform offer similar. Embed snippets work on WordPress, Webflow, Squarespace, Shopify, and custom HTML sites.
How do no-code form builders compare on price-per-submission?
At 1,000 submissions/month: Tally Pro $24 (unlimited) = $0.029. Formester Personal $13 (5,000 cap) = $0.0022. Fillout Starter $15 (1,000 cap) = $0.0038. Jotform Bronze $34 (1,000 cap) = $0.034. Typeform Plus $79 (1,000 cap) = $0.005. Formester wins on raw cost per submission at this scale; Tally wins if you're under 1,000.
Can a no-code form builder replace a developer?
For 95% of standard forms, yes. Lead capture, surveys, payment forms, RSVPs, internal intake are all faster to ship in Formester, Tally, or Jotform than to code from scratch. Developers become useful when you need custom validation logic, deep CRM workflows that go beyond Zapier, or pixel-perfect design on a marketing landing page.
